evidence.evidence_text: The Socratic method is a way of guiding students toward solving a problem independently without directly revealing the solution to the problem.
Large language models (LLMs) can be used to augment human effort by automatically generating Socratic questions for students.

To alleviate this problem, inspired by reinforcement learning with AI feedback (RLAIF), we first propose a data augmentation method to enrich existing Socratic questioning datasets with questions that are invalid in specific ways.
Next, we propose a method to optimize open-source LLMs such as LLama 2 to prefer ground-truth questions over generated invalid ones, using direct preference optimization (DPO).
